analysis:
The PR is a documentation-only change to docs/reference/configuration.md. It adds two table rows at head lines 415-416 (not visible in the supplied head excerpt, which starts at line 1 and is numbered up to 353; the patch hunk shows them). The rows document DARKBLOOM_TTFT_STREAM_TOOL_CALLS and DARKBLOOM_TTFT_THINK_CONTENT_SEED, both default-on and both forwarded to the LaunchAgent. No code or controls change in this PR, so I found no concrete security regression and no invalidated threat-model assumption. Security-relevant points for integration to confirm against the actual provider-swift source, which was not supplied:
1. Tool-call streaming (ToolStreamPreparation.streamsToolCallsByDefault) sends tool_call fragments before frame validation. The doc says each call is still validated when its frame closes. Fragments may already be emitted by then, so confirm that the E2E response encryption in TB-002/T-008 (fail closed, no plaintext SSE on encryption failure) applies to the streamed fragments, and that invalid calls cannot cause consumer-side misbehavior.
2. The think-content seed (ReasoningPromptProbe.seedsPlainTailContentByDefault) changes reasoning/content parsing. It could expose reasoning text as content in a mis-parse, but this is an output-formatting matter for the consumer's own data and does not cross a trust boundary.
The base excerpt (lines 519-686) is unchanged context. It documents the prefix cache (T-041), whose posture is not altered here. The new passthrough env vars are low-risk output-behavior toggles, not secrets or authorization inputs. Remaining uncertainty is whether the described code behavior matches the docs; this needs source review but is not evidenced as a vulnerability.
